overuse-injury.short: Damage that builds up from repeated loading, with no single moment of injury. Running shin pain after a mileage jump is one; a sprained ankle is not.

incidence.short: How many new injuries happen in a group over a stated amount of exposure, such as injuries per 1000 hours of running. Exposure in the bottom line makes groups comparable.

time-loss-injury.short: An injury counted only if the athlete misses training or competition. Simple to record, but it leaves out problems that you train through at a lower level.

hazard-ratio.short: A ratio of how fast events, such as injuries, happen in one group against another. HR 1.0 means no difference; HR 1.59 means a 59% higher rate.

bone-remodelling.short: The steady renewal of bone: cells remove small patches of old or damaged bone and other cells build new bone in their place. Training speeds it up.

microdamage.short: Tiny cracks that every load puts into bone. Remodelling normally repairs them. Damage that forms faster than it is repaired can add up to a bone stress injury.

cortical-bone.short: The dense, hard outer shell of a bone, such as the shaft of the shin bone. It makes up most of the skeleton's mass.

trabecular-bone.short: The spongy, lattice-like bone inside, found at the ends of long bones and in the pelvis and spine. Its large surface makes it quick to change.

tendinopathy.short: Pain and poor function in a tendon, brought on by load. It is a pain condition first: the tendon's look on a scan does not always match how it feels.

heavy-slow-resistance.short: Gym lifts with heavy loads, raised and lowered slowly, a few exercises a few times a week, with the weight raised over the weeks. Used to load tendons.

isometric-contraction.short: A muscle that tenses without changing length, like pushing against a wall or holding a half squat. Tendons carry load, but nothing moves.

tissue-capacity.short: How much repeated load a bone, tendon or muscle can take before damage outruns repair. It is raised slowly by training and falls with disuse or poor fuelling.

mechanical-load.short: The physical force put through a tissue, such as the impact through the shin at each footstrike. Distance and watts only estimate it.

proprioception-training.short: Balance and joint-position exercises, such as standing on one leg on an unstable surface. It trains the body's sense of where its joints are.
